title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Breakthrough in Brain Research
subtitle: Scientists win top honor for using light to control brain cells

summary.en: Three scientists have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine for their work in optogenetics. This field uses light to turn nerve cells on or off to study brain function. Researchers discovered how to use light-sensitive proteins from algae to control brain activity. This technology helps scientists understand complex conditions like depression and vision loss. The discovery is now used in laboratories around the world to solve brain mysteries.
summary.zh: 三位科學家因在光遺傳學領域的貢獻，榮獲2026年諾貝爾醫學獎。該領域利用光線開啟或關閉神經細胞，以研究大腦功能。研究人員發現如何利用藻類中的感光蛋白質來控制大腦活動。這項技術有助於科學家理解憂鬱症與視力喪失等複雜病況。該發現目前已在世界各地的實驗室中被用於解開大腦的奧秘。

paragraphs.en: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded to three scientists for their groundbreaking work in a field known as optogenetics. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel were honored for developing a tool that uses light to control nerve cells in the brain. According to MedPage Today, this discovery has opened a new era in neuroscience by allowing researchers to turn specific brain circuits on or off to see how they work.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年諾貝爾生理學或醫學獎頒給了三位科學家，以表彰他們在光遺傳學領域的開創性貢獻。戴瑟羅斯 (Karl Deisseroth)、黑格曼 (Peter Hegemann) 與納格爾 (Georg Nagel) 因開發出一種利用光線控制大腦神經細胞的工具而獲獎。根據《MedPage Today》報導，這項發現讓研究人員能夠開啟或關閉特定的腦部迴路，藉此觀察其運作方式，從而開啟了神經科學的新紀元。

paragraphs.en: For many years, scientists struggled to understand how different parts of the brain function. While they could study damaged brains or remove certain cells to see what happened, these methods were often limited. The brain is very flexible and can change its behavior if parts are missing. As Ars Technica reports, it is much more useful to activate or shut down neurons in an otherwise healthy brain. The work of these three scientists provides a way to do exactly that with great precision.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，科學家一直難以理解大腦不同部位的功能。雖然他們可以研究受損的大腦，或移除特定細胞來觀察變化，但這些方法往往受到限制。大腦具有高度靈活性，若部分缺失，其行為可能會發生改變。正如《Ars Technica》報導，在健康的大腦中活化或關閉神經元，其研究價值要高得多。這三位科學家的研究成果，正是提供了一種能以極高精確度達成此目標的方法。

paragraphs.en: The breakthrough began with the study of simple, single-celled green algae. Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel discovered that these tiny organisms move toward light because of a specific protein. When this protein is hit by blue light, it opens a channel that creates an electrical impulse. By putting this protein into other cells, researchers can make those cells react to light. Karl Deisseroth later built on this work, using the gene that controls this protein to create a light-controlled switch for nerve cells in the brains of living mice.
paragraphs.zh: 這項突破始於對簡單單細胞綠藻的研究。黑格曼與納格爾發現，這些微小生物因為一種特定蛋白質而會向光移動。當這種蛋白質受到藍光照射時，會開啟一個通道並產生電脈衝。透過將這種蛋白質植入其他細胞，研究人員能使這些細胞對光產生反應。戴瑟羅斯隨後在此基礎上進一步發展，利用控制該蛋白質的基因，為活體小鼠大腦中的神經細胞創造了一種光控開關。

paragraphs.en: "People usually think about light as a way of collecting information to observe things," Deisseroth explained to MedPage Today. "But this is the opposite of that. This is using light to control things, to make things happen, and to do it in a very precise way." Deisseroth developed tiny fibers to deliver light to these modified cells, allowing scientists to study how specific neural circuits influence behavior and disease.
paragraphs.zh: 「人們通常認為光是用來收集資訊以觀察事物的工具，」戴瑟羅斯向《MedPage Today》解釋道。「但這項技術恰恰相反。它是利用光來控制事物、促成變化，並且以非常精確的方式進行。」戴瑟羅斯開發了微小的光纖，將光線傳輸至這些經過改造的細胞，讓科學家得以研究特定的神經迴路如何影響行為與疾病。

paragraphs.en: This technology is now widely used in laboratories across the globe. Experts believe the impact of this research goes far beyond understanding a healthy brain. Abdel El Manira, a member of the Nobel Assembly, noted that optogenetics helps reveal how specific brain circuits are disrupted in various conditions. According to MedPage Today, these include serious health challenges such as blindness, depression, addiction, and dementia. Scientists are also exploring how these techniques might lead to new treatments for conditions like autism and schizophrenia.
paragraphs.zh: 這項技術目前已在全球各地的實驗室廣泛應用。專家認為，這項研究的影響力遠超於對健康大腦的理解。諾貝爾委員會成員艾爾馬尼拉 (Abdel El Manira) 指出，光遺傳學有助於揭示特定腦部迴路在各種病況下是如何受到干擾的。根據《MedPage Today》報導，這些病況包括失明、憂鬱症、成癮與失智症等嚴重的健康挑戰。科學家也正在探索這些技術如何能為自閉症與思覺失調症等疾病帶來新的治療方法。

paragraphs.en: Jeremy Berg, a researcher from the University of Pittsburgh, praised the work, noting that it provides a very precise set of tools for experiments that were previously almost impossible to perform. He recalled that when Deisseroth first proposed this vision in the early 2000s, it was a bold idea that eventually played out exactly as he predicted.
paragraphs.zh: 匹茲堡大學 (University of Pittsburgh) 的研究員柏格 (Jeremy Berg) 對這項研究給予高度評價，並指出它為過去幾乎無法進行的實驗提供了一套極為精確的工具。他回憶道，當戴瑟羅斯在2000年代初期首次提出這個願景時，這是一個大膽的想法，而最終的發展正如他所預測的那樣實現了。

paragraphs.en: Despite these major advances, the brain remains a complex organ with many secrets. El Manira stated that while we have made great progress, there is still much to learn. Optogenetics provides a powerful way to continue these studies and take on the challenges of understanding the human mind. For the scientists involved, the recognition is a highlight of decades of dedicated research.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管取得了這些重大進展，大腦依然是一個充滿許多秘密的複雜器官。艾爾馬尼拉表示，雖然我們已經取得了巨大進步，但仍有許多未知之處。光遺傳學提供了一種強大的方式來延續這些研究，並應對理解人類心智的挑戰。對於參與其中的科學家而言，這份榮譽是數十年奉獻研究生涯中的一大亮點。

paragraphs.en: For Karl Deisseroth, the news of the award came as a surprise. A self-described "night owl," he was working late at his home in Northern California when he received the call from the Nobel Assembly. He had just finished emailing students and was preparing to sleep when his life changed with the announcement of the prize.
paragraphs.zh: 對戴瑟羅斯來說，獲獎的消息令他感到驚訝。自稱是「夜貓子」的他，在北加州的家中熬夜工作時接到了來自諾貝爾委員會的電話。他當時剛寫完郵件給學生，正準備休息，沒想到獲獎的消息徹底改變了他的生活。

paragraphs.en: As the scientific community celebrates this achievement, the focus now shifts to how these light-based tools will be used in the future. While optogenetics is currently used mostly as a research technique, it is already being tested for medical purposes. For example, researchers are using a method called direct optogenetics to test a potential treatment for a genetic form of vision loss known as retinitis pigmentosa. As technology improves, the potential for new medical breakthroughs continues to grow, offering hope for patients suffering from brain-related diseases.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著科學界慶祝這項成就，焦點現在轉向這些光控工具未來將如何應用。雖然光遺傳學目前主要作為一種研究技術，但它已開始進行醫學用途的測試。例如，研究人員正利用一種稱為直接光遺傳學的方法，測試一種針對遺傳性視力喪失疾病「視網膜色素病變」的潛在療法。隨著技術進步，醫學突破的潛力持續增長，為患有腦部相關疾病的患者帶來了希望。

quiz.question: What specific biological mechanism allows the optogenetics technique to function?

options.A: The brain cells naturally produce proteins that react to blue light.
options.B: A protein from green algae creates an electrical impulse when exposed to blue light.
options.C: Tiny fibers are inserted into the brain to generate light-sensitive nerve cells.
options.D: The scientists use genetic modification to remove damaged brain circuits.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，科學家發現綠藻中的特定蛋白質在受到藍光照射時會開啟通道並產生電脈衝，這是光遺傳學技術的基礎。選項 A 錯誤，因為是大腦細胞被植入了該蛋白質，而非自然產生。選項 C 錯誤，光纖是用來傳輸光線的工具，而非製造細胞。選項 D 錯誤，文章並未提到移除電路，而是透過光線控制電路。

quiz.question: Why does the author suggest that studying damaged brains is less effective than using optogenetics?

options.A: Damaged brains are too dangerous for researchers to handle in a laboratory.
options.B: It is impossible to identify which specific brain cells have been damaged.
options.C: The brain's ability to adapt makes it hard to isolate the effects of a missing part.
options.D: Optogenetics is the only method that allows scientists to observe brain behavior.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第二段，傳統方法（如研究受損大腦或移除細胞）有其侷限性，因為大腦具有彈性（flexible），若缺失部分，大腦會改變行為，導致研究結果不準確。選項 A 文中未提及危險性。選項 B 並非主要原因，重點在於大腦的代償機制。選項 D 過於誇大，文章並未說這是唯一的方法，僅強調其精準度。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'the focus now shifts' imply?

options.A: The scientific community is changing its primary area of interest or attention.
options.B: Scientists are physically moving their laboratory equipment to new locations.
options.C: The Nobel Prize committee is changing the criteria for future awards.
options.D: Researchers are abandoning current experiments to start completely new projects.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，'the focus shifts' 意指研究重心或關注焦點的轉移。文章提到在獲得諾貝爾獎後，科學界將注意力從「技術開發」轉向「未來應用」，即如何將此工具用於醫療。選項 B 錯誤，這並非物理上的移動。選項 C 與文章內容無關。選項 D 錯誤，研究並未被拋棄，而是擴展到新的應用領域。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding optogenetics?

options.A: It is a historical discovery that has already cured most brain-related diseases.
options.B: It is a revolutionary tool that allows precise control of brain circuits with significant future medical potential.
options.C: It is a simple technique derived from algae that is mostly used for studying vision loss.
options.D: It is a controversial method that has caused debate among neuroscientists regarding its safety.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文主要介紹光遺傳學（optogenetics）如何利用光線精準控制腦神經，並強調其在研究大腦運作及未來治療腦部疾病（如憂鬱症、失智症等）方面的巨大潛力。選項 A 錯誤，目前尚在研究階段，並未治癒大多數疾病。選項 C 雖提到綠藻與視力喪失，但這僅是部分內容，非主旨。選項 D 錯誤，文中並未提到任何爭議或安全疑慮。
